name: Vitalik Buterin
milestone_by_age_26: Published the Ethereum white paper in November 2013 at age 19, proposing a Turing-complete smart contract platform that became the second-largest blockchain by market capitalization.
early_history_summary: Buterin emigrated from Russia to Canada at age 6, was placed in a gifted class in elementary school, and attended the private Abelard School in Toronto. He co-founded Bitcoin Magazine in 2011 at age 17, became deeply embedded in the cryptocurrency community, and conceived Ethereum after working on colored coins and other Bitcoin 2.0 projects. He dropped out of the University of Waterloo in 2014 after receiving a Thiel Fellowship to work on Ethereum full-time.
primary_leverage_engine: Technical depth in cryptography and game theory
family_context_summary: Born in Kolomna, Russia to Dmitry Buterin, a computer scientist, and Natalia Ameline, a finance professional. The family emigrated to Canada when Vitalik was six, seeking better employment opportunities.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a computer scientist and mother worked in finance, providing an intellectually rich household with exposure to both technical and financial thinking.
primary_early_advantage_tags: crypto community, Bitcoin Magazine, gifted education, immigrant drive, technical prodigy
evidence_summary: Buterin was placed in a gifted program in Canadian elementary school and attended a private high school, suggesting moderate educational resources. His father's computer science background likely influenced his technical interests. The decisive advantage was his early deep immersion in the Bitcoin community through Bitcoin Magazine and online forums, which gave him both technical knowledge and a distribution channel for his Ethereum vision. The Thiel Fellowship provided capital safety to drop out and focus full-time.
starting_point: Born in Kolomna, Russia to a computer scientist father and finance professional mother; family emigrated to Canada when he was six seeking better opportunities.
current_position: Co-founder and public face of Ethereum; net worth estimated in the hundreds of millions to low billions; resides in Singapore/Toronto.

trajectory.event: Co-founded Bitcoin Magazine, one of the first serious cryptocurrency publications.
Published the Ethereum white paper proposing a Turing-complete smart contract blockchain.
Received a Thiel Fellowship grant of $100,000 and dropped out of university to work on Ethereum full-time.
Ethereum blockchain launched with the mining of the genesis block on July 30.
Ethereum experienced the DAO hack, leading to a controversial hard fork that split the community.
Ethereum completed the London hard fork, introducing EIP-1559 fee burn mechanism.
Ethereum completed the Merge, transitioning from proof-of-work to proof-of-stake consensus.

name: Patrick Collison
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded Auctomatic, which was acquired for $5 million in 2008 at age 19, and then co-founded Stripe in 2010 at age 21, building what became the dominant online payments infrastructure company valued at over $70 billion.
early_history_summary: Collison grew up in Dromineer, County Tipperary, Ireland, the eldest of three boys in a family where both parents had scientific backgrounds. He took his first computer course at age 8 at the University of Limerick and began programming at 10. He won the BT Young Scientist of the Year competition at 16 in 2005 for developing a programming language and AI system. He attended MIT but dropped out after his first company, Auctomatic, was funded by Y Combinator and later acquired.
family_context_summary: Born to Lily Collison, a microbiologist, and Denis Collison, an electronic engineer, who later became entrepreneurs running a hotel and corporate training company. Grew up in the small village of Dromineer, County Tipperary, Ireland.
parent_family_domain_summary: Both parents had scientific backgrounds — mother in microbiology, father in electrical engineering — creating an intellectually rich household. Parents also demonstrated entrepreneurial behavior by running their own businesses.
primary_early_advantage_tags: sibling co-founder, scientific parents, early programming, Young Scientist, MIT, Y Combinator
evidence_summary: Collison benefited from scientifically educated parents who modeled entrepreneurship and provided early access to computing. The decisive advantage was the durable co-founder partnership with his younger brother John, which powered both Auctomatic and Stripe. His early recognition through the Young Scientist competition and admission to MIT provided elite institutional pipelines. The family's move to Silicon Valley positioned the brothers at the payments frontier.
starting_point: Born in Limerick, Ireland to a microbiologist mother and electronic engineer father who later became entrepreneurs; grew up in the small village of Dromineer, County Tipperary.
current_position: CEO of Stripe; net worth estimated at ~$17.5 billion per Forbes as of 2026; resides in California.

trajectory.event: Won the BT Young Scientist of the Year competition for a programming language and AI system.
Co-founded Shuppa/Auctomatic with brother John, funded by Y Combinator.
Auctomatic was acquired for $5 million.
Co-founded Stripe with brother John, building programmable financial infrastructure.
Stripe received $2 million in seed funding from Elon Musk, Peter Thiel, and Sequoia Capital.
Founded Fast Grants to accelerate COVID-19-related science funding with economist Tyler Cowen.
Co-founded Arc Institute, a nonprofit biomedical research organization.

name: John Collison
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded Auctomatic, which was acquired for $5 million in March 2008 at age 17, and then co-founded Stripe in 2010 at age 19, becoming the world's youngest self-made billionaire in 2016 at age 26.
early_history_summary: Collison grew up in Dromineer, County Tipperary, Ireland, the second of three boys in a scientifically minded family. He attended Harvard University to study physics but dropped out to work on Stripe with his brother Patrick in Silicon Valley. Before Harvard, he had already become a millionaire through the Auctomatic acquisition at age 17.
family_context_summary: Born to Lily Collison, a microbiologist, and Denis Collison, an electronic engineer, who later became entrepreneurs. Grew up in the small village of Dromineer, County Tipperary, Ireland, as the second of three brothers.
parent_family_domain_summary: Both parents had scientific backgrounds and demonstrated entrepreneurship by running their own businesses, creating an environment that valued both intellectual pursuit and business creation.
primary_early_advantage_tags: sibling co-founder, scientific parents, early programming, Harvard, Y Combinator, Silicon Valley
evidence_summary: Collison shared the same scientifically rich household as his brother Patrick, with both parents providing domain-relevant knowledge and entrepreneurial modeling. The most significant advantage was the durable co-founder relationship with his older brother Patrick, which powered both Auctomatic and Stripe. Harvard admission and the Y Combinator ecosystem provided elite institutional pipelines.
starting_point: Born in Limerick, Ireland to a microbiologist mother and electronic engineer father who later became entrepreneurs; grew up in the small village of Dromineer, County Tipperary.
current_position: President of Stripe; net worth estimated at ~$9.3 billion per Bloomberg as of 2026; resides in San Francisco.

trajectory.event: Co-founded Shuppa/Auctomatic with brother Patrick, funded by Y Combinator.
Auctomatic was acquired for $5 million in March, making him a millionaire as a teenager.
Co-founded Stripe with brother Patrick after dropping out of Harvard.
Became the world's youngest self-made billionaire after Stripe was valued at $5 billion.
Stripe reached a $20 billion valuation, cementing its position as a fintech leader.
Stripe was valued at $95 billion, making it the most valuable private fintech startup.

name: Palmer Luckey
milestone_by_age_26: Founded Oculus VR in April 2012 at age 19, launched the Oculus Rift on Kickstarter raising $2.4 million, and sold the company to Facebook for $2 billion in 2014 at age 21, reviving the entire virtual reality industry.
early_history_summary: Luckey grew up in Long Beach, California, homeschooled by his mother while his father worked as a car salesman. He began building VR headsets at age 16 in his parents' garage, completing his first prototype (PR1) at 17. He funded his projects by fixing and reselling damaged iPhones and working as a groundskeeper and youth sailing coach. He shared progress on the MTBS3D forum, building a community around his work. He attended Cal State Long Beach but dropped out to found Oculus VR.
primary_leverage_engine: Obsessive hardware tinkering and online community
family_context_summary: Born in Long Beach, California. Father Donald was a car salesman and mother Julie was a stay-at-home mom who homeschooled Luckey and his three younger sisters. The family was middle-class; Luckey self-funded his VR projects through odd jobs.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources. Father was a car salesman and mother was a homeschooling stay-at-home parent; neither had technology or engineering backgrounds.
primary_early_advantage_tags: garage tinkering, MTBS3D forum, self-funded, VR hardware prodigy, Kickstarter
evidence_summary: Luckey had no inherited financial or domain advantages — his father was a car salesman and mother a homeschooler. His advantage was entirely self-created: obsessive hardware tinkering from age 16, building 50+ VR headset prototypes in his garage, and leveraging the MTBS3D online forum as both a learning and distribution channel. The Kickstarter campaign validated market demand, and John Carmack's endorsement provided critical credibility.
starting_point: Born in Long Beach, California to a car salesman father and stay-at-home/homeschooling mother; grew up middle-class with three younger sisters.
current_position: Founder and CEO of Anduril Industries; net worth estimated at ~$3.6 billion per Forbes; resides in Newport Beach, California.

trajectory.event: Began building custom VR headsets in his parents' garage, funded by repairing and reselling iPhones.
Founded Oculus VR and launched the Oculus Rift Kickstarter, raising $2.4 million.
Sold Oculus VR to Facebook for $2 billion, becoming one of Silicon Valley's youngest self-made billionaires.
Departed Oculus/Facebook and co-founded Anduril Industries, a defense technology company.
Anduril reached a $4 billion valuation, establishing it as a major defense tech competitor.
Anduril raised $1.5 billion at a $14 billion valuation, cementing Luckey's status as a defense tech leader.

name: Austin Russell
milestone_by_age_26: Founded Luminar Technologies in 2012 at age 17, received a Thiel Fellowship in 2013, and took the company public via SPAC in December 2020 at age 25, becoming the world's youngest self-made billionaire.
early_history_summary: Russell grew up in Newport Beach, California, and demonstrated an early obsession with optics and photonics. He self-studied lidar and laser systems as a teenager, founding Luminar while still in high school at age 17. He attended Stanford University for three months to study applied physics before dropping out after winning the $100,000 Thiel Fellowship in 2013. Luminar operated in stealth mode from 2012 to 2017 before emerging with venture backing, developing long-range lidar sensors for autonomous vehicles.
primary_leverage_engine: Deep technical expertise in optics and lidar
family_context_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources. Russell grew up in Newport Beach, California, but family financial background and parental professions are not publicly detailed.
primary_early_advantage_tags: optics prodigy, Thiel Fellowship, Stanford, autonomous vehicle wave, lidar
evidence_summary: Russell's family background is not well documented in reviewed sources. His primary advantage was self-taught expertise in optics and lidar technology, developed as a teenager. The Thiel Fellowship provided capital safety to drop out of Stanford, and the Stanford/MIT ecosystem provided institutional credibility. The autonomous vehicle wave provided structural tailwinds for Luminar's lidar technology.
starting_point: Born in Newport Beach, California; family background not documented in reviewed sources.
current_position: Former CEO of Luminar Technologies, which filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in December 2025; was once the world's youngest self-made billionaire at age 25.

trajectory.event: Founded Luminar Technologies while still in high school, developing lidar sensors for autonomous vehicles.
Won a $100,000 Thiel Fellowship and dropped out of Stanford to focus on Luminar full-time.
Luminar emerged from stealth mode with venture capital backing.
Luminar went public via SPAC, making Russell the world's youngest self-made billionaire.
Began negotiating to become majority owner of Forbes, but the deal fell through in November.
Luminar filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy; Russell became subject of legal proceedings.

name: Boyan Slat
milestone_by_age_26: Founded The Ocean Cleanup in 2013 at age 18, after his TEDx talk went viral, and raised $2.2 million through crowdfunding from 38,000 donors in 160 countries to fund a feasibility study for ocean plastic removal technology.
early_history_summary: Slat grew up in Delft, Netherlands, and became interested in ocean plastic pollution at age 16 after a diving trip to Greece where he saw more plastic bags than fish. He developed the concept for a passive ocean cleanup system as a school project and presented it at TEDx Delft in 2012. When the talk went viral in early 2013, he dropped out of his aerospace engineering degree at TU Delft to found The Ocean Cleanup, assembling a volunteer team and launching a crowdfunding campaign.
primary_leverage_engine: Single-minded focus on a planetary problem
family_context_summary: Born and raised in Delft, Netherlands. Family background is not well documented in reviewed sources.
primary_early_advantage_tags: TEDx viral, crowdfunding, ocean plastic, TU Delft, Thiel Fellowship
evidence_summary: Slat's family background is not documented in reviewed sources. His advantage came from a direct personal experience with ocean plastic pollution during a diving trip, which gave him authentic domain proximity. The TEDx platform and subsequent viral spread provided distribution that would have been difficult to achieve through traditional channels. The crowdfunding campaign validated public demand and provided capital without traditional VC networks.
starting_point: Born in Delft, Netherlands; family background not documented in reviewed sources.
current_position: Founder and CEO of The Ocean Cleanup; recognized as the youngest UN Champion of the Earth; resides in the Netherlands.

trajectory.event: During a diving trip to Greece, saw more plastic than fish, inspiring his ocean cleanup mission.
Presented his ocean cleanup concept at TEDx Delft.
Founded The Ocean Cleanup after his TEDx talk went viral; raised $2.2 million via crowdfunding.
Published a 528-page feasibility study on ocean plastic cleanup.
Launched System 001, the first ocean cleanup system, from San Francisco into the Pacific.
The Ocean Cleanup deployed System 03, scaling up to clean the Great Pacific Garbage Patch.

name: Sam Bankman-Fried
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded Alameda Research, a quantitative crypto trading firm, in November 2017 at age 25, exploiting Bitcoin arbitrage opportunities between Japan and the US to generate tens of millions in profits within months.
early_history_summary: Bankman-Fried grew up on the Stanford University campus, the son of two Stanford Law School professors. He studied physics and mathematics at MIT, where he was involved in the effective altruism community. After graduating, he worked as a quantitative trader at Jane Street Capital for three years before leaving to found Alameda Research in 2017, recruiting about 20 young effective altruists to execute crypto arbitrage strategies.
primary_leverage_engine: Quantitative trading expertise and elite networks
family_context_summary: Born to Joseph Bankman and Barbara Fried, both Stanford Law School professors. Grew up on the Stanford campus in an affluent academic household immersed in legal and philosophical discourse.
parent_family_domain_summary: Both parents are Stanford Law professors, providing elite academic networks and intellectual environment. The family subscribed to utilitarian philosophy, which influenced SBF's effective altruism approach.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Stanford professor parents, MIT, Jane Street, effective altruism network, crypto arbitrage
evidence_summary: Bankman-Fried grew up in an elite academic environment with two Stanford Law professor parents, providing both intellectual modeling and access to elite networks. MIT and Jane Street Capital further concentrated opportunity. The effective altruism community provided a ready-made team of recruits for Alameda Research. His later conviction for fraud in the FTX collapse does not negate the material milestone achieved by age 25.
starting_point: Born in Stanford, California to two Stanford Law School professors; grew up on the Stanford campus in an affluent academic household.
current_position: Incarcerated at Federal Correctional Institution, Lompoc I; sentenced to 25 years in prison for fraud related to the collapse of FTX and Alameda Research in November 2022.

trajectory.event: Graduated from MIT with a degree in physics and minor in mathematics; began trading at Jane Street Capital.
Co-founded Alameda Research to exploit crypto arbitrage opportunities, particularly the Bitcoin price gap between Japan and the US.
Co-founded FTX, a cryptocurrency derivatives exchange, in Hong Kong.
FTX raised funding at a $25 billion valuation; SBF ranked among the richest Americans on Forbes 400.
FTX collapsed in November; filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy; SBF arrested in December.
Convicted on seven counts of fraud and conspiracy.
Sentenced to 25 years in federal prison.

name: Alexandr Wang
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded Scale AI in 2016 at age 19, admitted to Y Combinator, and built it into a unicorn valued at $7.3 billion by 2021, becoming the world's youngest self-made billionaire at age 24.
early_history_summary: Wang grew up in Los Alamos, New Mexico, the son of Chinese immigrant physicists who worked at the Los Alamos National Laboratory. He was passionate about math and programming from childhood, qualifying for the Math Olympiad Program and US Physics Team in high school. He worked full-time at Quora at age 17, where he met his future co-founder Lucy Guo. He briefly attended MIT before dropping out to co-found Scale AI through Y Combinator's accelerator program.
primary_leverage_engine: Technical depth in math and machine learning
family_context_summary: Born in Los Alamos, New Mexico, to Chinese immigrant parents who were both physicists at the Los Alamos National Laboratory. Growing up in a national lab town where 'everybody's parent is some sort of scientist' shaped his scientific orientation.
parent_family_domain_summary: Both parents were physicists at Los Alamos National Laboratory, providing direct exposure to scientific thinking and a culture of technical excellence in a community saturated with researchers.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Los Alamos physicists, Math Olympiad, MIT, Y Combinator, Quora, AI wave
evidence_summary: Wang grew up in the unique environment of Los Alamos, New Mexico, surrounded by scientists at the national laboratory where both his parents worked as physicists. This provided a science-saturated community and domain-relevant parental modeling. His early recognition through Math Olympiad and US Physics Team qualifications, combined with full-time engineering work at Quora at 17, gave him both technical depth and practical experience. The Y Combinator ecosystem and the AI/ML structural wave were critical amplifiers.
starting_point: Born in Los Alamos, New Mexico to Chinese immigrant parents who were both physicists at Los Alamos National Laboratory; grew up in a science-saturated community.
current_position: Chief AI Officer at Meta Platforms (since June 2025); former CEO of Scale AI; net worth estimated at ~$3.6 billion per Forbes as of 2025.

trajectory.event: Qualified for the US Math Olympiad Program and US Physics Team.
Co-founded Scale AI with Lucy Guo after dropping out of MIT; admitted to Y Combinator.
Became the world's youngest self-made billionaire after Scale AI raised $325 million at a $7.3 billion valuation.
Scale AI raised $1 billion in Series F at a $13.8 billion valuation.
Meta acquired 49% of Scale AI in a ~$29 billion deal; Wang became Meta's Chief AI Officer.

name: Shayne Coplan
milestone_by_age_26: Founded Polymarket in June 2020 at age 22, building a blockchain-based prediction market that became one of the world's largest prediction platforms, and became the world's youngest self-made billionaire at age 27 in 2025.
early_history_summary: Coplan was born and raised on the Upper West Side of Manhattan, raised by his mother and attending public schools in Hell's Kitchen. He became interested in cryptocurrency as a teenager, becoming the youngest participant in the 2014 Ethereum crowdsale at approximately age 16. He briefly attended NYU for computer science before dropping out. He worked on early crypto projects including TokenUnion and Union Market before pivoting to found Polymarket during the COVID-19 pandemic in 2020.
family_context_summary: Born into a Jewish family in 1998 and raised on the Upper West Side of Manhattan in New York City. He was raised by his mother and attended public schools in Hell's Kitchen. Family financial details are not documented.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources beyond being raised by his mother in Manhattan.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Ethereum crowdsale, crypto community, NYC, prediction markets, self-taught
evidence_summary: Coplan's family background is minimally documented; he was raised by his mother in Manhattan and attended public schools. His key advantage was extraordinarily early immersion in the cryptocurrency ecosystem — participating in the 2014 Ethereum crowdsale as a teenager and building crypto projects from his late teens. The online crypto community served as his primary learning and network channel. NYC provided proximity to finance and media ecosystems that later amplified Polymarket's reach.
starting_point: Born in 1998 in New York City to a Jewish family; raised by his mother on the Upper West Side of Manhattan; attended public schools in Hell's Kitchen.
current_position: Founder and CEO of Polymarket; became the world's youngest self-made billionaire in October 2025 with an estimated net worth of ~$1 billion per Forbes; resides in New York City.

trajectory.event: Participated in the Ethereum crowdsale as its youngest participant.
Founded Polymarket, a blockchain-based prediction market platform, from his Lower East Side apartment.
Polymarket gained mainstream attention during the US presidential election with billions in trading volume.
FBI raided Coplan's New York apartment in November as part of a DOJ investigation.
Became the world's youngest self-made billionaire after a $2 billion investment from ICE valued Polymarket at ~$14 billion.

name: Laura Deming
milestone_by_age_26: Founded The Longevity Fund in 2011 at age 17, the first venture capital firm dedicated to funding aging and life-extension biotech companies, after being named a Thiel Fellow and dropping out of MIT at age 14.
early_history_summary: Deming grew up in New Zealand, where she was homeschooled and developed an interest in the biology of aging at age 8. At age 12, she emailed renowned aging researcher Cynthia Kenyon at UCSF and joined her lab, prompting her family to move to the US. She matriculated at MIT at age 14 to study physics, then dropped out at 17 to accept the Thiel Fellowship and start The Longevity Fund, becoming one of only two women in the inaugural 2011 Thiel Fellow class.
primary_leverage_engine: Obsessive early focus on longevity science
secondary_engine: Elite lab access and Thiel Fellowship
family_context_summary: Daughter of John and Tabitha Deming; grew up in New Zealand where she and her brother were homeschooled. The family relocated from New Zealand to the United States to enable her lab work at UCSF, a significant commitment.
parent_family_domain_summary: Parents were not scientists but supported her scientific interests through homeschooling and a cross-country move to enable lab access, demonstrating exceptional educational commitment.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Cynthia Kenyon lab, MIT at 14, Thiel Fellowship, homeschooling, longevity prodigy, family relocation
evidence_summary: Deming's extraordinary trajectory was enabled by her family's willingness to relocate from New Zealand to San Francisco to support her research interests, and by Cynthia Kenyon's willingness to mentor a 12-year-old in a university biogerontology lab. Access to a frontier research lab at age 12 provided rare early tools and facilities. Her admission to MIT at 14 and the Thiel Fellowship at 17 provided elite institutional pipelines. Her self-taught background in calculus and statistics, combined with lab experience, constituted exceptional prior reps for her age.
starting_point: Born in New Zealand to John and Tabitha Deming; homeschooled with her brother; family relocated to the US to support her scientific career.
current_position: Partner at The Longevity Fund and co-founder of age1, a $55 million longevity-focused VC fund; also CEO/co-founder of Until, a biotech research company; resides in San Francisco.

trajectory.event: Joined Cynthia Kenyon's biogerontology lab at UCSF after emailing her directly.
Matriculated at MIT to study physics.
Accepted as a Thiel Fellow; dropped out of MIT and founded The Longevity Fund.
Closed The Longevity Fund's second fund at $22 million.
Co-launched age1, a $55 million next-generation longevity VC fund with Alex Colville.

name: Simon Tian
milestone_by_age_26: Founded Neptune in January 2013 at age 18, launched the Neptune Pine smartwatch on Kickstarter raising over $800,000 in 30 days, and was named a 2015 Thiel Fellow, with the device shipping by August 2014 and becoming available through Best Buy and Amazon.
early_history_summary: Tian was born to Chinese Canadian parents in Montreal, Quebec, and attended a French school in La Prairie. He started Neptune in January 2013 while still studying at Marianopolis College, posting conceptual drawings of a smartwatch online before building a prototype or incorporating. He received over 20,000 pre-orders within weeks, then traveled to China to meet contract manufacturers. The Kickstarter campaign reached its $100,000 goal within 27 hours and ultimately raised over $800,000. He dropped out of high school at 18 to pursue Neptune full-time.
family_context_summary: Born to Chinese Canadian parents in Montreal, Quebec. Raised in Brossard, a suburb of Montreal. Family financial background is not documented in reviewed sources.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources beyond being Chinese Canadian parents in Montreal.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Kickstarter, smartwatch, Thiel Fellow, self-taught, crowdfunding, early product launch
evidence_summary: Tian's family background is minimally documented. His advantage was primarily self-created: he identified the smartwatch trend early, used online product launches and Kickstarter as distribution channels, and leveraged the Thiel Fellowship for capital and credibility. The decision to drop out of high school at 18 to pursue hardware entrepreneurship represents a constraint-driven path. His fluency in English, French, and Mandarin facilitated work with international contract manufacturers in China.
starting_point: Born in 1994 in Montreal, Quebec to Chinese Canadian parents; raised in Brossard, a suburb of Montreal; attended French-language schools.
current_position: Founder and CEO of Neptune, a consumer electronics and wearable technology company; based in Montreal, Canada.

trajectory.event: Founded Neptune and posted conceptual smartwatch drawings online, receiving 20,000+ pre-orders before building a prototype.

Named a Thiel Fellow, receiving $100,000 to pursue Neptune full-time.

name: Blake Resnick
milestone_by_age_26: Founded BRINC Drones in 2019 at age 18 (initial work began at 17 in 2017), received a Thiel Fellowship in 2020, was named the youngest honoree on Forbes 30 Under 30 in 2022, and raised a $25 million Series A in 2021 at age 21, building a drone company valued at $300 million by 2023.
early_history_summary: Resnick grew up in Las Vegas, born to a doctor and a special education teacher. He started college at UNLV at age 14, where he built a fusion reactor in his garage. He interned at McLaren, Tesla, and DJI as a teenager, developing engineering skills. After the 2017 Las Vegas mass shooting, he cold-called the Las Vegas SWAT commander to understand what technology could have helped, then dropped out of Northwestern University at 17 to develop drone technology for first responders, founding BRINC.
primary_leverage_engine: Hardware engineering depth and customer obsession
family_context_summary: Born in Las Vegas to a doctor father and special education teacher mother. The family was middle-class; Resnick has dyslexia, which made traditional education challenging and motivated his early college enrollment at 14.
parent_family_domain_summary: Parents were a doctor and a special education teacher — not directly in technology or engineering, but providing a stable, educated household that supported his unconventional educational path.
primary_early_advantage_tags: dyslexia, early college, fusion reactor, Tesla internship, SWAT customer, Thiel Fellowship
evidence_summary: Resnick's parents were a doctor and special education teacher — middle-class professionals but not in tech. His dyslexia created friction with traditional education, motivating him to start college at 14 and drop out of high school. He self-taught electrical engineering via YouTube and built a fusion reactor in his garage at 14. The decisive advantage was his direct customer immersion: cold-calling the Las Vegas SWAT commander and working with them to develop the first BRINC drone. The Thiel Fellowship provided capital safety and credibility.
starting_point: Born in 2000 in Las Vegas to a doctor father and special education teacher mother; has dyslexia; started college at age 14.
current_position: Founder and CEO of BRINC Drones; company valued at $300+ million with ~110 employees; raised over $82 million in total funding; resides in Seattle.

trajectory.event: Started college at UNLV and built a fusion reactor in his garage.

name: Awais Ahmed
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded Pixxel Space Technologies in February 2019 at age 20-21, building India's first private hyperspectral satellite company, and was named to Fortune India 40 Under 40 in 2022 at age 23-24, with Pixxel launching its first satellites and securing a NASA contract.
early_history_summary: Ahmed grew up in Aldur, a small village in Karnataka's Chikkamagaluru district, without internet access until 8th grade. His father brought home encyclopedias on space and science. At BITS Pilani, he studied mathematics and manufacturing engineering, joined a student satellite team working with ISRO scientists, and was a founding member of Hyperloop India, which became a finalist at the SpaceX Hyperloop Pod Competition. He founded Pixxel in his final year of undergraduate studies, dropping his dual degree to focus on the company.
primary_leverage_engine: Space technology domain immersion and competition experience
family_context_summary: Born in Aldur, a small village in Chikkamagaluru district, Karnataka, India. Parents are Nadeem Ahmed and Ghazala Tashfeen. Grew up without internet access until 8th grade; his father provided encyclopedias on space and science.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father brought home encyclopedias on space and science, nurturing early interest in space technology despite the family's remote location and limited digital access.
primary_early_advantage_tags: village upbringing, no internet, encyclopedias, BITS Pilani, ISRO, SpaceX Hyperloop, space tech wave
evidence_summary: Ahmed grew up in a village without internet access until 8th grade, with his father providing encyclopedias as a window to space science. This resource constraint created a distinctive drive. BITS Pilani provided the elite institutional pipeline, and the student satellite team with ISRO scientists gave rare early exposure to satellite development. The SpaceX Hyperloop Pod Competition provided international validation. The emerging Indian private space sector post-2019 provided a structural wave for Pixxel.
starting_point: Born in Aldur, a small village in Karnataka, India; grew up without internet until 8th grade; father brought home encyclopedias on space and science.
current_position: Founder and CEO of Pixxel Space Technologies; company has raised ~$95-100M from Google, Lightspeed, and others; launched nine hyperspectral satellites including six in 2025; first Indian space startup to secure a NASA contract; leads a team of 275.

trajectory.event: Co-founded Hyperloop India, which became a finalist at the SpaceX Hyperloop Pod Competition in Los Angeles.
Co-founded Pixxel Space Technologies with Kshitij Khandelwal in February, while in final year at BITS Pilani.
Named to Fortune India 40 Under 40 list; Pixxel launched its first hyperspectral satellites.
Pixxel raised $36 million from investors including Google.
Pixxel launched six hyperspectral satellites and secured a NASA contract for Earth-observation data.

name: Luana Lopes Lara
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded Kalshi in 2018 at age 22 with Tarek Mansour, entered Y Combinator's Winter 2019 batch, and built the first federally regulated prediction market exchange in the United States, later becoming the world's youngest self-made woman billionaire at age 29.
early_history_summary: Lopes Lara was born in Belo Horizonte, Brazil, the daughter of a math teacher and an engineer. She trained as a ballerina at the Bolshoi Theater School in Santa Catarina and performed professionally in Austria for nine months before deciding to pursue technology. She moved to the US at 17 to study computer science and mathematics at MIT, where she met her co-founder Tarek Mansour.
